subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Shipping Container
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Shipping Container usable.

hook.text: In 1956, a trucker loaded 58 metal boxes onto a ship. That simple idea changed the entire world.

buildup.text: Before containers, loading a ship took weeks. Dockers moved cargo piece by piece—slow and costly.

discovery.text: Malcolm McLean's standardized container cut loading time from weeks to hours and costs by 90%.

twist.text: Ports resisted at first. Unions fought it—containers eliminated thousands of dockworker jobs.

climax.text: Today, 90% of world trade moves in containers. Globalization rests on a steel box.

punchline.text: A metal box made the global economy possible.

quiz.question: What did the shipping container reduce?
